claim: For every pair of integers \(n,t\ge1\), there exists a literal-systematic code \(E(x)=x\Vert p(x)\) from \(\mathcal A^n\) to \(\mathcal A^{n+t+1}\) that corrects every contiguous deletion burst of length at most \(t\), using \(t+1\) deletion-prone trailer symbols, whenever the alphabet size \(q\) is a power of two with \(q>2(n+t+1)^2+1\); the least such power of two satisfies \(q<4(n+t+1)^2+2\).
scientific_limitations_integrity: Existence proof via a finite conflict graph and an independent transversal.
No pointwise efficient encoder or uniform construction is established.
No optimality claim is made for the alphabet size or for \(t+1\) trailers when \(t>2\).
The result is distinct from fixed-alphabet bit-redundancy bounds for nonsystematic codes.
title: Quadratic-alphabet existence for systematic burst-deletion codes
